div.head: ECf 32 C 8
div.ab: Erat enim predictus rex Ine optimus largus, sapiens et prudens et moderatus, strenuus, iustus et animosus, bellicosus pro loco et tempore, et in diuinis legibus et secularibus institutis, scriptis et bonorum operum exhibitionibus irradiat, gloriosus rexit, qui regnum et confederauit et consolidauit et in unum pacificauit sapiencia et prudencia magna et, ubi locus adfuit, ui et manu armata.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 659 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 …”, so it is kept with ECf here.
Liebermann prints the words taken from the Prologue of Hn (prudens, moderatus, iustus, in diuinis legibus … irradiat, gloriosus) in smaller type.

note.seg: solchen Charakter schenkt der Londoner auch beliebigen anderen Königen: mein Leges Angl. S. 45. Hier stiehlt er Heinrichs I. Lob
the Londoner bestows such a character on any other kings too: my Leges Angl. p. 45. Here he steals the praise of Henry I
so; irradiauit glor., rexitque r. Ld
so; irradiauit glor., rexitque r. Ld

div.ab: For the aforesaid King Ine was most excellent, generous, wise and prudent and moderate, vigorous, just and courageous, warlike as place and time required, and in divine laws and secular institutions, in writings and in displays of good works he shines; he ruled gloriously, who bound together and united the kingdom and pacified it as one by great wisdom and prudence and, where occasion arose, by force and armed hand.
